milestone: the A1 scorer had two defects, and both of them moved the number
result: (1) The key's phrases were matched against normalised text while the phrases themselves were not, so a net name written 'relay_ctrl' could never match 'RELAY_CTRL' in a finding: a real detection scored as a miss. (2) The clean-bill test was a substring search, and it fired on 'the flyback diode IS CORRECT under a convention' and on 'the 2N2222A is BYPASSED', turning a board the overlooker had refused to send to a fab into a FALSE PASS. Fixed, and the key was split: words that name the FAULT detect, words that name the PART are a near miss, and a wrong value is now caught by stating the specified value and a different one - a rule from the defect, not from any one run's wording. 19 new tests on the scorer (37 in all, 1 skipped until the set is complete).

milestone: the seventh calibration case: mains_gap, a mains-to-SELV clearance fault
result: The last case needed a mains-carrying board and the product has no mains template, so the builder laid the mains domain by hand on top of the product's own board. MAINS_L runs 0.35 mm from the DHT22_DATA net, where the base board has 5.85 mm. The product's verifier returns ok=True on the defective board and KiCad's own DRC is identical on both: a false pass, declared as one. The 5.0 mm requirement is quoted from IEC 60664-1 Table F.4 and is NOT qualified by anyone; the geometry is exact. That gap is owner decision D1.

milestone: the A1 scorer grew a rule for a clearance fault, and the key with it
result: A phrase list cannot catch 'mains-to-SELV creepage is 0.35 mm' in every wording, the same way it could not catch a wrong capacitance. So the scorer can now read a MEASURED GAP: a finding that measures a space and finds it under 2 mm has named the fault. The number has to be a gap and not a feature - a track width is not a clearance - and a number that belongs to a configured rule ('the 0.2 mm clearance rules are set to zero') is not a measurement of the board. A full stop between digits is a decimal point, not a sentence end; the clause splitter was reading 0.35 mm as 0 and 35. 8 new tests on the scorer (45 in all, none skipped).
